quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What shape is a speed limit sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road, and you must follow them.

questions.question: If a dog chases you on your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. The body gets rid of 1 drink per hour. How many drinks are left in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. The person drank 7 drinks and 6 hours have passed (3 hours drinking + 3 hours after). So 7 minus 6 equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main things affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and food intake also matter. But how often you normally drink does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is at the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Can a motorcycle with a sidecar tip over?

options.text: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharp or go too fast through a corner.

questions.question: What is the best formation when riding through curves or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is normally best for group riding. But when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway, riders should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Occupy your friend with activities to distract them from drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired friend ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, or find an excuse to keep them from leaving until they are sober. Ask other friends to help.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Provides protection for the eyes and face.
Does not protect the face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection for the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield protects your eyes and face the most. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you don't have to wear eye protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet so you can focus on riding. They should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit close to you without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Brake on the tire that is not flat.
Brake on the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly brake on the tire that is not flat (if you know which one it is).

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your vehicle before you move.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should it be positioned?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intention, check for traffic, and only pass when it is safe. Signal again and move back to your original lane when you can.

questions.question: What should a face shield NOT be to work properly?

options.text: Allowing clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, let you see to both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: They should lean together at the same angle.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays straight.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while you keep your body upright.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles. Laced boots work best. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict is at intersections. Be extra alert when another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They will definitely yield to you.
They might not actually see you.
It is not worth your effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: They might not actually see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for groups. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Successful motorcyclists know they are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seen by other motorists.
questions.explanation: You are safest when other drivers can clearly see you. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and lane position to stay visible.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, a horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.
Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes motorcycles take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: It is recommended that a motorcyclist:

options.text: Change power suddenly in a turn.
Ride the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before a turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn, not during it.

questions.question: If you are riding when it starts to rain, it is a good idea to:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that make it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight that affects handling. Your motorcycle will need extra space to stop completely.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is harder to see than a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing suddenly so other drivers notice it, especially if you are stopping faster than they expect.

questions.question: Which of the following will best protect your eyes from wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide this protection.

questions.question: To provide the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: In a no passing zone, what can a motorcycle do?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it can finish before another vehicle comes.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by driving off the road.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and hurt handling. Put loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the front from tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check all of these except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, do a complete check of your motorcycle. Check the tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the rider.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Use the owner's manual as your main source of information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before riding for the first time.

questions.question: Cold tablets and similar common drugs:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
Usually do not affect your ability to safely ride.
Pose no risk to safe riding.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: When riding on bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may make your motorcycle weave slightly. This is usually safe, so stay calm and cross at a steady speed. Zigzagging is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider begins to pass.
Let several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and return to formation before the next rider starts to pass.

questions.question: Flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will slow down where drivers don't expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down where drivers don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it. Flash it when slowing down unexpectedly, like mid-block or near an alley.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts occur between motorcyclists and other drivers. Use extra caution when entering and crossing intersections.
